article_lead.description: an asymmetric link for binary event probabilities that can express multiplicative changes in a no-event or hazard scale

new_bank_questions.title: Complementary log-log probability update
new_bank_questions.body: A complementary log-log model has baseline event probability 0.20. A one-unit covariate change has coefficient log(2). Find the new event probability and state which quantity doubles.
new_bank_questions.answer: Write H=-log(1-p). Initially H=-log(0.8). The coefficient doubles H, so 1-p_new=exp(-2H)=0.8^2=0.64 and p_new=0.36. The negative log of the no-event probability doubles; the event probability does not.

new_bank_questions.title: Reading a complementary log-log coefficient
new_bank_questions.body: In a binary cloglog regression, a coefficient is log(3). What exactly is multiplied by three, and when can it be called a hazard ratio?
new_bank_questions.answer: The quantity -log(1-p), where p is the fitted event probability, is multiplied by three. A hazard-ratio interpretation additionally requires a suitable proportional-hazards model for event times; an arbitrary cross-sectional binary response does not supply that interpretation. Neither the odds nor probability generally triples.

new_bank_questions.title: Reversing the event in a cloglog model
new_bank_questions.body: A fitted complementary log-log model describes event probability p. Does negating its coefficients give the same-link model for the nonevent probability 1-p? Explain.
new_bank_questions.answer: No. The inverse cloglog curve is asymmetric, so reversing the outcome changes the link to its log-log counterpart; simple coefficient sign reversal is the logit's symmetry. Refit or transform the model explicitly for the chosen event definition.
